label: Run 1 (2026-10-20)
status: NOT a valid comparison of the three arms: two of them were hobbled by defects of the harness, and the numbers below must not be read as a comparison of the policies.
halted: the free tier returned HTTP 429 (free-models-per-day) after the first model; the other two planned models were not run
tokens_note: The runner of run 1 had `tokens = 0` hard-coded (commit 64266c1), so the token columns of this run are empty.  A live probe of the same endpoint on 2026-10-20 confirmed that the server does report the usage (`usage.prompt_tokens` and `usage.completion_tokens`), so the zeros were a defect of the runner and not of the provider.  The runner counts the tokens since then.
wall_clock_note: The `wall_seconds` of the committed payload of run 1 was 0.  The time the calls really took is the sum of the per cell seconds: it is reported below as the measured time.

defects.title: The simple-retry arm threw away the work the model had done.
defects.evidence: The runner wrote the files of an answer only when the claim said "completed".  The sandbox of `simple-retry/natural/task01-harbour` holds only `notes.md`, while the sandbox of `naive/natural/task01-harbour` holds all four files of the same task, with the same model.
defects.effect: The baseline scored worse than doing nothing (0.100 against 0.400).  This is the anomaly the maintainer flagged.
defects.fix: Every arm now writes the files of every answer, whatever the claim says.  `tests/test_trial_arms.py` pins it down.

defects.title: The prompt never told the model that `progress` is a number from 0 to 100.
defects.evidence: The contract of AgenTether treats a completed step with a progress below 100 as drift.  The attempt log of `agentether/natural/task03-lantern-memory` reads: "Context drift at step 'notes': step was reported as completed but progress is 1 (expected='progress >= 100 for a completed step', observed=1.0)".  The second and the third step of that task were never even attempted.
defects.effect: The agentether arm was rejected on steps the other two arms accepted.  Its rate measures the prompt, not the library.
defects.fix: The prompt states the scale of `progress` and that it must be 100 for a completed step.  The change was applied to every arm.

defects.title: The roadmap order stopped the agentether arm at the first failed step.
defects.evidence: The orchestrator refuses a step whose predecessors are not completed.  The other two arms walk through every step whatever happened.
defects.effect: The two arms did not even make the same number of calls for the same task.
defects.fix: The trial builds the orchestrator with `strict_order=False` and closes the breaker again before every step, so each step gets the same number of attempts as in the other arms.

defects.title: The injected fault schedule was keyed on a counter that ran across the whole task.
defects.evidence: `fault_for(task_index, step_index, attempts)` was called with the cumulative number of attempts of the task, so an arm that retried more met different faults for the same step.  The claim that every arm saw the same faults was therefore false.
defects.effect: The injected condition was not paired.
defects.fix: The schedule is a function of the task, the step and the attempt number *inside* that step.

defects.title: The belief of the arms was computed three different ways.
defects.evidence: The naive arm took the status of the last answer, the simple-retry arm remembered that *any* step had ever completed, and the agentether arm took the status of the last step.
defects.effect: The false completion rate was not comparable between the arms.
defects.fix: Every arm now reports a verdict for every step, and the belief of the task is true when every step was considered done.

defects.title: The token accounting was hard-coded to zero and the wall clock of the payload was 0.
defects.evidence: The runner of run 1 had `tokens = 0` in the body of the loop, and the committed payload has `wall_seconds: 0` next to `requests: 291`.
defects.effect: The overhead of the arms could not be reported in tokens.
defects.fix: The runner counts the tokens of the usage the server reports, sums the time of the calls, and seeds the counters of a resumed run with the cells of the earlier sessions.
